stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of a Nahua account in the Florentine Codex (16th century), public domain; compiled by Bernardino de Sahagun with Nahua scholars.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of a Nahua account of smallpox in Tenochtitlan, recorded in the Florentine Codex, compiled by the Franciscan friar Bernardino de Sahagun with Nahua scholars in the 1500s. The account describes the sick lying in their houses and sleeping places, no longer able to move or stir, while the healthy could not bury the dead fast enough. Whole neighborhoods fell ill at once.

stem: The Nahua account describes the sick lying unable to move while the healthy could not bury the dead. What does this detail best show about the smallpox epidemic in Tenochtitlan?

options.text: The Spanish deliberately poisoned the city's water supply to spread the disease.
options.misconception: Smallpox spread by contact, not by poisoned water, and it ran ahead of the soldiers.

options.text: Smallpox spread only among Mexica rulers and priests, not ordinary people.
options.misconception: The account says whole neighborhoods fell ill, not only rulers and priests.

options.text: The Mexica had no medicine of any kind before the Spanish arrived.
options.misconception: The Mexica had healers and medicines; the problem was a new disease, not no medicine.

options.text: The epidemic struck so many at once that burial broke down.

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
